conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** **Yes**, substantial empirical evidence confirms that Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy effectively alleviates symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

### Key Evidence Supporting EMDR

1. **Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses**
   * **Equivalent Efficacy to CBT:** Cochrane systematic reviews evaluating psychological therapies for chronic PTSD demonstrate strong support for the efficacy of EMDR, finding its effectiveness comparable to trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (TF-CBT) (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD003388_psychological-therapies-chronic-post-traumatic-stress-disorder-ptsd-adults).
   * **First-Line Treatment Status:** Updated systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) recommend EMDR alongside TF-CBT as a primary, first-line psychological intervention for adults with PTSD (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32284821/).

2. **Endorsement by Health Organizations**
   * **Clinical Guidelines:** Major health authorities, including the American Psychological Association (APA), officially suggest and recommend EMDR as a structured treatment for PTSD (https://www.apa.org/ptsd-guideline/treatments/eye-movement-reprocessing).
   * **Global and Veteran Health Recommendations:** Guidance from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs/Department of Defense (VA/DoD) similarly recognize EMDR as an effective, evidence-based trauma intervention for adults when administered by trained clinicians (https://www.gromeus.com/psy/various-psy/emdr-therapy-ptsd-evidence/).

In summary, clinical trials and international practice guidelines consistently establish EMDR as a reliable, highly effective therapy for treating PTSD symptoms.
